questions.question: A GitHub Actions workflow must deploy to Azure without storing a client secret. What should you configure?

options.text: A federated credential on a managed identity, and the azure/login action with OpenID Connect
options.why: Correct. The workflow proves its identity with an OIDC token, so no secret is stored.

options.text: A client secret in repository secrets
options.why: This stores a secret that can leak and expire.

options.text: A storage account key in the workflow file
options.why: A key in a file is a stored secret and is unsafe.

options.text: A shared administrator password
options.why: This is a stored credential with excessive access.

questions.explanation: Workload identity federation removes stored secrets.

questions.question: A pipeline must stop a release when a prompt change lowers answer groundedness. What should you add?

options.text: An evaluation step with a groundedness threshold that fails the job
options.why: Correct. The evaluation gate blocks promotion when scores are too low.

options.text: A step that sends an email after release
options.why: It informs but does not stop the release.

options.text: A larger model deployment
options.why: A bigger model does not stop a weak change.

options.text: A longer pipeline timeout
options.why: Timeouts do not measure quality.

questions.explanation: An evaluation gate is a release control based on measured quality.

questions.scenario: A team keeps Foundry resources, projects and deployments in source control and wants identical environments for dev, test and prod with different capacity.
questions.question: Which approach meets the requirement?

options.text: A copy of the production resource group made manually each time
options.why: Manual copies drift and are hard to review.

options.text: Bicep templates with a parameter file for each environment
options.why: Correct. The same template deploys each environment with its own values.

options.text: Portal clicks recorded in a document
options.why: This is not repeatable or reviewable.

options.text: One shared project for all environments
options.why: This removes isolation between environments.

questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code gives repeatable environments.

questions.question: What should a federated credential for the production deployment job be tied to?

options.text: A personal access token
options.why: This is a stored credential tied to a person.

options.text: Any workflow in the organisation
options.why: This is far too broad.

options.text: The protected prod environment of the repository
options.why: Correct. The approval rules on the environment apply before Azure issues a token.

options.text: Any branch in the repository
options.why: This lets unreviewed code request production access.

questions.explanation: A narrow subject claim limits which runs can sign in.

questions.question: How should a tested agent change reach production?

options.text: Promote the same tested definition through test to prod, with approval
options.why: Correct. This keeps what was tested identical to what is released.

options.text: Rebuild the agent by hand in prod
options.why: This risks differences from the tested version.

options.text: Edit the prod agent directly and test afterwards
options.why: Customers would see untested changes.

options.text: Skip dev to save time
options.why: This removes the first test stage.
